Model: Cage exchange - male in a previously male occupied cage

Model: Modafinil-induced wakefulness
Effect: Promotes wake at expense of other sleep states, large dose = efficiently longer wake. Strongly induced Fos in TMN and orexin neurons of the PFx
Other effects: may promote waking via activation of TMN and orexin neuron

Model: Dose dependent use of caffeine
Effect: A dose-dependent and significant prolongation of sleep onset latency
Other effects: effect was sensitive to zolpidem and trazodone, both of which attenuated the caffeine-induced increase in SOL

Model: Dose dependent use of caffeine
Effect: 12.5+25mg/kg: Increased wakefulness, decreased total sleep time. 0.125+1.25mg/kg: increased SWS1 at expense of SWS2

Model: Diazepam IP injections in different doses (to treat sleep apnea)

Model: Expose rodents to auditory/tactile stimulus
Effect: Caused sleep fragmentation
Author: Polotsk

Author: Qu

Model: Using SeCl14 to block prostaglandin D synthase (PGDS) on H-PGDS KO mice.

Author: Qu

Model: DP1R antagonist ONO-4127Na infused into subrachnoid space(200pmol/min)
Effect: Reduced NREM by at max 30% and REM by max 60, increased wakefulness

Other effects: iron deficient less red blood cells

Model: Ntsr1 knockout mice

Model: Sleep patterns in different levels of anxiety in mice strains
Effect: High anxiety needed more sleep, due to heavy sleep fragmentation, lower quality of sleep. Had a drive for REM sleep.

Model: ICV infusion of orexin-A

Model: ICV infusion of orexin-B
Effect: Dose-dependent increase in wakefulness and decrease in NREM and REM sleep
Author: Akanmu

Model: Injections of orexin-A/hcrt1 in LC

Model: Striatial excitotoxic lesion

Author: Cui

Model: Injections with PCPA and sleeping in different temperatures(20,30,32)

Model: Acute cocaine through IP of three doses (3.6, 9.6, 18 mg/kg)

Author: Bjorness + Greene

Author: Bjorness

Model: Cocaine abstinence after chronic cocaine use
Effect: Increase in arousal for about 2 weeks. Increase in gamma energy Sleep latency increased.
Other effects: SWS SWE and W SWA remained elevated during early portion and increase in SWS during latter portion. Reduction in waking during early and middle DP
Author: Bjorness

Model: Heterozygous amino acid substitution at S246 to alanine in Hdac4

Model: Heterozygous alanine substitution at Thr221 in Sik3 gene

Model: Deletion of Sik3 in vglut2-positive neurons

Model: Deletion of Sik3 in vglut1-positive neurons

Author: Kim

Model: Deletion of Sik3 in vgat-positive neurons
Effect: Decrease in total REM sleep time

Model: Inhibition of dDpMe/vIPAG GABAergic neurons

Author: Chen

Model: Global KO of Kcnn2 and Kcnn3
Effect: Kcnn2/3 KO sleep duration decreased (approx. -2,2h and approx. -1.85h). Awake state stabilization. Kcnn2 sig. decrease NREM

Model: Global KO of Cacna1g and Cacna1h
Effect: Significant decrease in sleep duration (approx- 1,4h and -1.5h resp), short-sleeper phenotype (SD?)
Author: Tatsuki

Model: Global KO of Camk2a and Camk2b
Effect: Significant decrease in sleep duration (approx- 0.9h and -2.0h resp).
Other effects: Camk2b KO less likely to transition from wake-sleep and sleep-wake.
Author: Tatsuki

Model: IP injection of PCP and MK-801 (NMDARs antagonists)
Effect: Decreased sleep duration. MK-801 sign. decrease of NREM sleep duration. Short-sleeper phenotype (SD?)
Author: Tatsuki

Model: Global KO of Nr3a gene
Effect: Decreased sleep duration (approx. -1,55h). Wakefulness stabilized due to decreased transitions from awake to sleep states.

Author: Sunagawa

Model: Whole body deletion of Erk1
Effect: Significantly increased duration of wakefulness in both

Author: Mikhail

Model: neuro-specific deletion of Erk2
Effect: Significantly increased duration of wakefulness and significant decrease in  NREM sleep.
Other effects: After SD, wakefuless was increased and NREM decreased
Author: Mikhail

Author: Mikhail

Model: Selective activation (AL-OXB) of OXR2 in orexin KO mice by ICV

Other effects: Ameloriate narcolepsy symptoms. Continious ICV injection make it last for 12h, decrease during dark phase. Didn't trigger reward pathways, less chance of addiction.
Author: Yamamoto

Model: Activation of orexin neurons using orexin-A in orexin KO mice
Effect: Increased wake time and wake bout duration 3h after injection, reduced wake-NREM transition frequency. REM also suppressed (not sig)
Other effects: Ameloriate narcolepsy symptoms. Continious ICV injection make it last for 12h, decrease during dark phase. Did trigger reward pathways - more chance of addiction
Author: Yamamoto

Model: Activation of PVH arginine vasopressin neurons (SSFO)
Effect: Immediate wakefulness from both NREM+REM, last 20-30min. Induced transitions to wake from NREM+REM.
Other effects: SSFO high specificity and efficency. Some leaked expression of SSFO to neighbouring nuclei
Author: Islam

Model: Activation of PVH arginine vasopressin neurons
Effect: Increased time spent in wakefulness (+148,3%) and reduced NREM+REM (-45.9% and -59.2%)
Other effects: Sleep quality not changed after activation. Lasted for approx 7h. Activation ncreased number of c-fos-pos LHox
Author: Islam

Model: Activation of PVH AVP projection neuronal fibers in LH
Effect: Induced awakefulness for ~25min. Rapidly induced transitions to wakefulness from both NREM+REM
Other effects: Orexin receptor antagonist suvorexant during activation drastically shortened duration of induced wake
Author: Islam

Model: Administration of melanotan-II (melanocortin receptor agonist)
Effect: Significantly increased wakefulness and reduced NREM+REM(-44.7 and -86.1%). During 3h, wake increased +164.1%
Other effects: Sleep quality not altered after administration.
Author: Islam

Model: Tfa2b+/- mice
Effect: Female show increased wakefulness and NREM sleep decreased, mainly during DP
Other effects: Decreased delta power during NREM sleep. Male exhibited a slight increase in EEG power during NREM.
Author: Nakai

Model: Generate Tfap2b mutant mouse strain
Effect: K114/K144 male reduced NREMS time (esp DP) and episode of wake was significantly increased
Author: Nakai

Model: Generate Tfap2b mutant mouse strain
Effect: K145/+ female episode number incr. and duration decr, of NREM during LP. Episode numbers of wake and REM also increased.
Author: Nakai

Model: Tfap2b deleted in nervous system during development
Effect: Increased wakefulness and decreased NREM sleep (episode number, esp LP). Circadian rytm deficits
Other effects: Increase in EEG power during wakefulness
Author: Nakai

Model: Tfap2b deleted postnatally by administrating tamoxifen
Effect: Decreased NREM sleep and increased wakefulness, esp during DP.
Other effects: Exhibit normal response to SD
Author: Nakai

Model: central 5-HT neuron ablation in mice using diphteria toxin + receptors
Effect: Decreased REM duration (-24.7%), fewer transitions from NREM-REM (-34.7%). Attenuated wake respnse to novel environment
Other effects: Increased theta power during wake. Decreased NREM sleep episode duration during DP.
Author: Iwasaki

Model: Specific mutations at S551 site in SIK3 gene (S551A/D)
Effect: Increased sleep need; increased NREMS amount and longer episodes, reduced wake. Hypersomnia, sleepy during day
Other effects: Elevated delta power during NREMS. S551A also a little less REM, increased low-frequency during wake
Author: Honda

Model: GLUT1 deficency syndrome mouse model using ENU i.p.
Effect: Longer wake times, shorter NREMS time.
Metabolic side effects: Reduced BW, glucose transport reduced, glucose metabolism increased, increased locomotion
Other effects: Homozygous are embryonic lethal. Decreased CBS fluid glucose value, convulsize seizures
Author: Furose

Model: Loss of Gscl gene homologous recombinition using ES cells
Effect: Reduced REMS time and fewer REMS episodes. REM sleep latency increased. Slight increase in total NREM. Less NREM-REM transitions
Other effects: Also lacked expression of Dgcr14 in IP. Reduced theta power during REMS and increased arousability during REMS. Reduced REMS rebound
Author: Funato

Model: Knock-out of MEf2D gene
Effect: Altered circadian rythm, with the sleep-cycle happened later during the day. . Fragmented sleep, sig. shorter REM latency. More transitions wake<->NREM.
Other effects: delayed activity onset (~25min) than WT and longer free-running period during dark(+40min). Also fragmented activity in comparison to WT. Clock gene expression normal.
Author: Mohawk

Model: Overexpression of orexin in transgenic mice line
Effect: Fragmentation+reduced REM duration and latency.NREM decrease. Increase wake. incomplete REM sleep atonia
Author: Willie

Model: Inhibiting LS GABAergic neurons (bipolar disorder mouse model)
Effect: Reduced sleep and heightened arousal.
Other effects: Increased irritable behaviour.
Author: Zhou

Model: Ablation of LS GABAergic neurons using casp3
Effect: Significant  increase in arousal and reduction in sleep. Sig. increase in wake and NREM episodes, while REM episodes decreased. Increase in NREM to wake and wake to NREM transition.
Other effects: Took longer to enter NREM after 6 hours of SD. Increased irritable behaviour.
Author: Zhou

Model: Activation of excitatory neurons in mPFC
Effect: Increased wakefulness duration.
Author: Honjoh

Model: 6 hour sleep deprivation by introducing novel objects and cage change
Effect: Increased wakefulness. Increased gamma and theta frequency in EEG, delta reduced. Cortical activation.
Other effects: Increased sleep pressure.
Author: Honjoh

Model: Activation of astrocytes in the pons
Effect: Strongly suppressed REM sleeep due to increased episode numbers. Increased NREM sleep due to increased duration. Decreased transitions from wake to NREM, NREM to REM and REM to wake.
Other effects: Increased delta waves
Author: Kurogi

Model: Activation of cortical neurons during NREM and REM sleep
Effect: Always woke mice up from NREM and REM sleep. REM needed more light stimulation.
Author: Mao

Model: Activation of cortical neurons during NREM and REM sleep
Effect: Always woke mice up from NREM and REM sleep. REM needed more light stimulation. More effective in PtA (less light stimulation needed)
Author: Mao
